Class NlsKeyMapper

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.nls.NlsKeyMapper
public final class NlsKeyMapper extends Object
Translates a raw NLS property key into the form the client addresses it by.

The backend and the frontend derive their key from the same camelCase field name, but by different mechanical rules: the backend uses RestHelper.camelCaseToDotSeparated() (readableName to readable.name) because that is what MessageSource resolves server-side, while the frontend uses AppHelper.toUpperCaseWithUnderscore() (readableName to READABLE_NAME) because that is what TranslateService resolves. This class is the bridge that lets a single properties entry serve both lookups.

The rules are ordered and the order is significant:

  1. "c." - strip the prefix and emit the remainder verbatim. Marks a key that is consumed only by the client and is never resolved server-side, such as a dynamic-form validator message. The prefix exists because shape alone cannot separate the two dialects: webUrl is simultaneously a real server-resolved Bean Validation message (see grafiosch.validation.WebUrl) and a frontend validator key with a different text, so c.webUrl yields the client key webUrl while the server-side webUrl yields WEBURL.
  2. A registered pass-through prefix (g., gt., UDF_) - emit verbatim, because those keys name configuration parameters and metadata rather than being derived from a field name.
  3. A registered nested namespace - split on the first dot only and emit a one-level object.
  4. Everything else - upper-case and replace dots with underscores.

Rule 4 is idempotent on keys that are already UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, which is what allows a key to be moved from the frontend translation files into a properties file unchanged. Note that it must not key off "contains a dot": roughly two dozen field labels (name, date, email, isin, ...) are single lower-case words that still have to become UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.

      public static final String CLIENT_PREFIX
